dashboard.purpose: Evidence-first recruiter/research hybrid: understandable in under one minute while retaining enough detail for a technical reviewer to audit the result.

screenshot_specification.contact_sheet: 5 screenshots on one labeled review sheet; all text must be readable at review scale.

implementation_rules: Step-5 preview images are reference-only. Final figures, dashboard, video, manuscript, screenshots, and animations must be programmatically generated from the frozen Step-4 release data and the approved Step-5 design contract. Preview images must not be used as backgrounds, flattened canvases, stock imagery, or composited substitutes for the actual coded artifacts.

limitations.required_public_language: The A/B/C profiles form a controlled toy example with five instances per model and one relevant item per instance. The result demonstrates that a ranking reversal can occur under the frozen sampling protocol; it does not estimate how often or how strongly this occurs in production recommender systems.
limitations.required_sensitivity_language: Sensitivity conclusions are restricted to the predefined sample-size grid. When a relation changes between adjacent computed values, the project reports that interval and does not infer an exact uncomputed crossover.

narrative: Open with the engineering/evaluation question, not the paper.
Show the m=99 sampled AP ordering.
State that the underlying A/B/C rank profiles did not change.
Use AUC to prevent the claim from becoming 'all sampling is bad'.
Mention independent analytical + Monte Carlo validation.
Close with the practical lesson: validate evaluation protocols.
linkedin.preferred_hook: I kept the models fixed and changed only the evaluation protocol. The AP model ordering changed.

figure_1.layout: Two-panel ranked-dot comparison. Left panel: full-catalog AP. Right panel: expected sampled AP at m=99. Profiles A/B/C use fixed colors. Each panel prints its tie-aware ordering above the chart. A center annotation states that the underlying rank profiles are unchanged while the evaluation protocol changes.
figure_1.purpose: Show the central replicated result immediately.
figure_1.question: Does the full-catalog AP ordering agree with expected sampled AP at m=99?
figure_1.required_callout: Full AP: C>B>A | Expected sampled AP (m=99): A>B>C
figure_1.title: Sampling can reverse the AP model ordering

figure_2.layout: Three vertically aligned small multiples for AP, NDCG, and Recall@10. X-axis uses the exact frozen m grid on a log-like categorical/log presentation. Y-axis shows expected metric value. Profiles A/B/C retain fixed colors. Computed-grid crossover intervals may be shaded or annotated only when present in the frozen release data.
figure_2.purpose: Show that the m=99 result is part of a broader sample-size sensitivity pattern without inventing uncomputed thresholds.
figure_2.question: How do expected sampled metrics evolve across the predefined sample-size grid?
figure_2.title: The ordering depends on how many negatives are sampled

figure_3.layout: Upper panel: AUC across the frozen m grid, emphasizing its agreement with full-catalog AUC. Lower panel: analytical expectation versus high-precision Monte Carlo means for A/B/C and retained public metrics, with MC SE shown only where visually legible. Supporting validation details remain in the evidence table.
figure_3.purpose: Prevent overgeneralization while showing validation rigor.
figure_3.question: Is the observed behavior metric-specific, and do the independent computational paths agree?
figure_3.title: AUC is the negative control; simulation validates the analytical result
